uncited: It differs from [Naive Isosurface Extraction](4328-naive-isosurface-extraction.md) by guaranteeing domain coverage without requiring a global mesh, and from [Adaptive Octree Marching Tetrahedra](3897-adaptive-octree-marching-tetrahedra.md) by using local stencils rather than hierarchical subdivision for surface approximation.
*   **Input:** A set of scattered data points $P = \{p_i\}$, where each point has a 3D position and a scalar function value $f(p_i)$.
**Binning Grid:** A regular grid of size $2^{l_b} \times 2^{l_b} \times 2^{l_b}$ cells, where $l_b$ is the binning grid level.
**Local Tetrahedrization:** A Delaunay tetrahedralization of the Stencil Point Set.
*   Traverse the octree in a depth-first fashion.
*   Append the level of any node reached that contains at least one empty child node to a list $L$.
*   If a leaf cell is encountered (a node containing only empty children), add its level to $L$.
*   Fill empty cells of the binning grid with a single data point at the center of the cell.
Determine its function value by interpolating using the original data points.
*   The union of the stencil tetrahedrizations covers the box formed by the outer layer points, which contains the domain of the data points.
The local tetrahedrizations are generated on-the-fly, avoiding global mesh construction costs.
It addresses the limitations of global tessellation and resampling methods for scattered data, which can introduce biases or lose context.
